newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end at 38-month low on labour fears.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end at 38-month low on labour fears.

text.p: Stocks closed at the lowest levels in 38 months on Thursday in depressed trading caused by fears of labour strife over the government's plan to revise labour laws, brokers said.
The composite index ended 9.57 points lower at a provisional 706.30, the lowest since September 25, when it closed at 703.55.
"The escalating confrontation between labour groups and the government scares investors," said Kim Won-suk, a broker at Dongwon Securities.
Union groups object to the articles that open the way to worker layoffs and flexible working hours.

Daewoo shares fell only slightly and mainly in line with the general market decline after a French government decision to suspend the sale of Thomson SA. The Daewoo Group had been in line to take over Thomson's consumer electronics group.
Daewoo Electronics fell 250 won to 6,080 and Daewoo Telecom dropped 240 won to 9,460.
On Wedensday, members of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions voted overwhelmingly to strike to protest at the government's labour reform plan.

The confederation said its members represented major workplaces, including Hyundai Motor, the nation's largest carmaker, Kia Motors, Hyundai Heavy Industries and Daewoo Heavy Industries. It claims membership of around 500,000.
Brokers said a nation-wide labour unrest would be a serious blow to the already staggering market.
They said the banking industry may face large-scale layoffs if the government prosals becomes laws.
Berokers said banks might have to merge to cope with the industry's opening to wider foreign competition and many jobs could be made redundant.
They forecast the market would fall further on Friday.
"It is hard to say now where the bottom will be," said Kim Heung-shik, a broker at Hyundai Securities.
